questions.question: A half turn measures 180°. Ravi splits it into 4 equal parts, so each part is 45°. His angle is made of 3 of those parts. He draws both of its arms only 2 cm long. Using 45°, 90° and 180° as references, about how big is Ravi's angle?
options: About 135°, an obtuse angle
About 45°, an acute angle, because both arms are only 2 cm long
About 90°, a right angle
About 180°, a straight angle
questions.explain: Three of the four 45° parts make 45° + 45° + 45° = 135°, which is between the 90° and 180° references, so it is obtuse. Short arms are a trap — arm length never changes how far an angle opens.

questions.question: A right angle measures 90°. Mia opens her angle exactly half as wide as a right angle, and she draws both of its arms 8 cm long. Using 45°, 90° and 180° as references, about how big is Mia's angle?
options: About 90°, a right angle, because arms as long as 8 cm make a wide opening
About 45°, an acute angle
About 135°, an obtuse angle
About 180°, a straight angle
questions.explain: Half of the 90° reference is 45°, so the angle is acute — smaller than a square corner. The common trap is thinking long 8 cm arms make the angle bigger; only the amount of opening counts.

questions.question: A half turn measures 180° and can be split into 4 equal parts of 45° each. Deja's angle is made of 2 of those parts, and she draws her arms 9 cm long. Kwan's angle is made of 3 of those same parts, but he draws his arms only 1 cm long. Whose angle is bigger?
options: Deja's, because her arms are 9 cm and Kwan's are only 1 cm
They are the same size, because both angles come from the same half turn
Kwan's, because 3 parts of 45° make about 135°, while Deja's is about 90°
Deja's, because 2 parts of 45° make 135°
questions.explain: Count the 45° parts: 2 parts is 90°, a right angle, and 3 parts is 135°, an obtuse angle, so Kwan's is bigger. Do not compare the arms — a 1 cm arm can hold a much wider opening than a 9 cm arm.

questions.question: A straight angle measures 180° and can be split into 4 equal parts of 45° each. Priya's angle is made of just 1 of those parts, but she draws its arms 12 cm long, stretching right across her page. About how big is Priya's angle?
options: About 90°, a right angle
About 135°, an obtuse angle
About 180°, a straight angle, because the 12 cm arms stretch across the whole page
About 45°, an acute angle
questions.explain: One of the four 45° parts is 45°, which is less than the 90° reference, so the angle is acute. Drawing the arms 12 cm long only makes it look bigger — the opening is still 45°.

questions.question: At the Coquitlam skate park, the angle between a ramp and the flat ground opens about half as much as a square corner. The ramp surface itself is 4 m long. Using 45°, 90° and 180° as references, which is the best estimate for that angle?
options: About 45°, an acute angle
About 80°, an acute angle that is nearly a square corner
About 135°, an obtuse angle
About 90°, a right angle, because a 4 m ramp is long and long sides make big angles
questions.explain: Half of the 90° reference is 45°, so the ramp angle is acute. The 4 m length of the ramp surface is a distraction — how long a side is has nothing to do with how wide the angle opens.

questions.question: Maya opens her laptop until the screen leans back a bit past a square corner, but it is still far from lying flat on the table. The screen is 30 cm tall. Which is the best estimate for the angle between the screen and the keyboard?
options: About 45°, because the 30 cm screen is short
About 115°, an obtuse angle
About 180°, a straight angle
About 90°, a right angle
questions.explain: A bit past the 90° reference but nowhere near the 180° reference means the estimate belongs between them, around 115°, an obtuse angle. The height of the screen does not matter — only how far it has swung open.

questions.question: Ben has no protractor and needs to estimate an angle that looks a little wider than a square corner. Which method gives the best estimate?
options: Decide it must be 45°, because any angle that is not a perfect square corner is half a right angle
Measure how long the two arms are — the longer the arms, the bigger the angle
Compare it with the square corner of a sheet of paper: it is a bit more than 90° but well under 180°, so about 100° to 110°
Decide it must be 180°, because both arms start from the same point
questions.explain: The 45°, 90° and 180° references let you judge an opening with no protractor: just past a square corner means a bit more than 90°. Measuring the arms tells you nothing — an angle with tiny arms can be far wider than one with long arms.

questions.question: Four angles are drawn in Ben's notebook with their measures labelled: 40°, 85°, 130° and 175°. The 130° angle is drawn with much longer arms than the other three. Which angle is best described as ‘almost a straight angle’?
options: The 40° one, because it is close to the 45° reference
The 85° one, because it is close to the 90° reference
The 130° one, because it is drawn with the longest arms
The 175° one, because it is only 5° away from 180°
questions.explain: A straight angle is 180°, so the measure closest to it is 175°. Compare each measure with 45°, 90° and 180° to see which reference it sits near; how long the arms are drawn is never part of that comparison.

questions.question: A camping chair's back starts standing straight up, making a right angle with the seat. Noor pushes the back down by about half a right angle. Using 45°, 90° and 180° as references, what is the new angle between the seat and the back, and what kind of angle is it?
options: About 135°, an obtuse angle
About 90°, still a right angle, because the seat itself has not moved
About 135°, but it is acute because the chair back is only 60 cm long
About 45°, an acute angle
questions.explain: Start at the 90° reference and add half a right angle: 90° + 45° = 135°, which is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse. Pushing the back away opens the angle wider, and the length of the back has no effect on it.

questions.question: A ferry leaves Horseshoe Bay heading north. It turns right by about half a right angle, sails on for a while, then turns right by about half a right angle again. Compared with its starting direction, about how far has the ferry turned in total, and what kind of angle is that?
options: About 45°, an acute angle, because both turns were the same size
About 90°, a right angle
About 180°, a straight angle, because two turns always make a half turn
It depends on how far the ferry sails between the turns — the longer it sails, the bigger the angle
questions.explain: Add the two turns: 45° + 45° = 90°, a quarter turn, so the ferry now faces east. The distance sailed between the turns changes nothing — like arm length, it does not affect how much the direction has swung.

questions.question: Nadia looks at two shapes on the classroom wall. A long thin pennant flag has two sides 30 cm long meeting at a very sharp point. A small square sticky note has sides 5 cm long meeting at a corner. Nadia says the flag's point must be the bigger angle because its sides are much longer. Is she right?
options: Yes, sides of 30 cm make a much bigger angle than sides of 5 cm
Yes, because the flag's point is sharp, and sharp angles are the largest
No — the sticky note corner is a right angle of 90°, while the sharp point is well under 45°, so the corner is bigger
No, they are equal, because every angle made by two straight sides is 90°
questions.explain: Judge an angle by how far it opens, not by how long its sides are: a square corner sits exactly on the 90° reference, and a very sharp point is far below the 45° reference. Long sides can hold a tiny angle, and short sides can hold a wide one.

questions.question: At a Richmond night market, Ken's paper fan makes a straight angle of 180° when it is fully open. He closes it until the opening is only one third of what it was. The fan sticks are 25 cm long. Which estimate and description are both correct?
options: About 120°, an obtuse angle, because the 25 cm sticks are long
About 60°, an obtuse angle, because 60 is more than 45
About 90°, a right angle, because one third of a straight angle is a quarter turn
About 60°, an acute angle, because it lies between the 45° and 90° references
questions.explain: One third of 180° is 60°, which sits between the 45° and 90° references, so it is still acute — obtuse means more than 90°, not more than 45°. The 25 cm sticks are a distraction, since stick length does not change how wide the fan opens.
